content: The Misuse of Drugs Act in Singapore is a national law designed to regulate and control the use of drugs. It categorizes controlled substances into three distinct classes: Class A, Class B, and Class C. Under Section 44 of the Act, the Minister has the authority to amend these classifications by issuing an order published in the Gazette. This allows the addition, removal, or reclassification of drugs within these categories. The penalties prescribed under this law are considered extremely severe by international standards. They include lengthy prison sentences, corporal punishment in the form of caning, and even capital punishment for certain offenses. For example, the possession of 30 grams of cannabis can result in the death penalty. The law also establishes a presumption of possession if an individual has keys to premises where drugs are found. Furthermore, any person found in or fleeing from a location that is proven or presumed to be used for drug consumption or administration is presumed to have been involved in drug use unless proven otherwise. This makes it highly risky to associate with individuals who use drugs. The Act grants law enforcement officers significant powers. They are permitted to search premises and individuals without a warrant if they have reasonable suspicion that controlled drugs or items subject to seizure are present. Additionally, under Section 31, officers are authorized to demand urine samples from individuals suspected of drug offenses. Section 17 of the Act specifies the threshold quantities of controlled drugs that, if exceeded, result in a presumption of drug trafficking unless the individual can prove otherwise. These thresholds are as follows: Opium: 100 grams Morphine: 3 grams Diamorphine (Heroin): 2 grams Cannabis: 15 grams Cannabis mixture: 30 grams Cannabis resin: 10 grams Cocaine: 3 grams Methamphetamine: 25 grams 10 grams of any combination of the following substances: N,α-dimethyl-3,4-(methylenedioxy)phenethylamine α-methyl-3,4-(methylenedioxy)phenethylamine N-ethyl-α-methyl-3,4-(methylenedioxy)phenethylamine It is important to note that the possession, consumption, manufacturing, import, export, or trafficking of these and other controlled substances in any quantity is strictly prohibited unless explicitly authorized by the government.
